Thank you for your pull request.
Give it a Conventional Commit title, for example "fix: reject CSV files with no rows".
CONTRIBUTING.md explains the workflow and the quality gates.

## Summary

<!-- What does this change, and why? Link the issue it solves, for example "Closes #12". -->

## Type of change

- [ ] `feat`: a new feature
- [ ] `fix`: a bug fix
- [ ] `docs`: documentation only
- [ ] `test`: tests only
- [ ] `refactor`: a code change that does not change behavior
- [ ] `perf`: a change that makes the code faster or use less memory
- [ ] `ci`: CI workflows
- [ ] `build`: dependencies, packaging or the Docker image
- [ ] `chore`: other maintenance

## How was this tested?

<!-- The commands you ran (for example make check) and anything you checked by hand. -->

## Checklist

<!-- Tick each item that is true. If one does not apply, say why. -->

- [ ] make check passes locally
- [ ] Tests added or updated for the change
- [ ] Coverage is still at least 95%
- [ ] No new noqa or type: ignore without a written reason
- [ ] Follows the Power of Ten rules in docs/CODING_STANDARD.md
- [ ] LEARNING.md / README updated if behavior changed
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md Unreleased section updated
- [ ] No secrets, keys or personal data committed
